properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-30, asking it directly of his own long-standing idea: *"I've wanted to design a 'mini-house' that is like a biodome and is as self-sufficient and recycles waste, etc — again, what is the 'domain' of this design and what should its artifacts be."*

⭐ THE QUESTION MAY BE THE FINDING. A self-sufficient habitat is not one domain. It is at least: architecture (envelope, thermal, structure), environmental and mechanical engineering (water reclamation, greywater and blackwater, air, HVAC), energy (generation, storage, load), agriculture or biology if it grows food, and controls. Asking which ONE it is has no true answer.

`Project.domain` is a single scalar, and `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` already records that it is WRITTEN AND NEVER READ. If it is ever made to drive anything — which is option (c) of dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-project-that-is-not-software — then a project spanning five disciplines is the case that breaks a scalar field on its first real outing. Cheap to notice now, expensive to notice after something reads it.

═══ WHAT THE ARTIFACTS PROBABLY ARE, offered as a starting list to be corrected ═══

· A MASS AND ENERGY BALANCE — water in/out/recovered, air, nutrients, power generated against power drawn. For a closed-loop habitat this is the artifact that matters most, because the failure that actually hurts is a loop that does not close.
· Loop schematics for water, waste and air (the process-engineering P&ID shape).
· Architectural plans for the envelope, and a thermal model.
· A growing plan, if it feeds anyone — species, area, yield, nutrient cycle.
· A controls and monitoring specification.
· Code and regulatory compliance — septic and greywater rules are usually the binding constraint on "recycles waste", far more than any engineering limit.

⭐ AND ONE OF THOSE IS ALREADY NEARLY REFLOW2'S. `Flow`, `Resource` and budget `Constraint` (`quantity` / `limit` / `direction`, with their CONSTRAINS spenders) are close to a mass-and-energy balance already, and the SV-7 measures/budgets viewpoint renders one — with an honest verdict of `incomplete` when any contribution is unstated. FOR A CLOSED-LOOP DESIGN, "incomplete because somebody has not said what this loop returns" IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE THE TOOL COULD SAY. That is not a new feature; it is existing machinery pointed at a domain nobody has pointed it at.

═══ AND THE REGULATORY HALF IS DESIGNED AND UNBUILT ═══
`dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built` says in as many words that the Environment / EnvironmentRule layer *"is what makes 'design a house' concrete"*. The biodome and the garage are both that unbuilt half. Two of the three cases Anthony named land on the same missing piece, which is worth more than either case alone.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══
(a) DOMAIN STAYS ONE FIELD and a multi-discipline project picks its dominant one. Simplest; loses exactly the projects most worth having.
(b) DOMAIN BECOMES A SET. Honest to reality; every computation that reads it then has to decide what to do when two domains disagree, which is a real cost and not obviously worth paying.
(c) DOMAIN IS NOT ON THE PROJECT AT ALL — discipline belongs to the PART, not the whole, since the envelope is architecture and the water loop is process engineering within one design. Closest to how the work is actually divided, and the largest change.
(d) DELETE IT, per `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` — a distinction nothing reads should be made real or removed, and nothing reads this one today.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any of this is worth doing before somebody actually starts a non-software design in reflow2. The garage is the nearest real candidate and it is Alex's, not Anthony's, so the evidence would be a second user's again.
properties.name: OPEN — the biodome has no single domain, and `Project.domain` is one field. Is asking "what domain is this?" the wrong question?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill, separately from dec:idea-who-authors-the-domain-artifact because these are two different questions — that one asks who holds the pen, this asks whether "the domain" is even a well-formed question for a design that spans five disciplines. Recorded as open rather than as a requirement: the artifact list is a starting point offered for correction by the person who actually wants the thing built, and the four options change the schema in ways nobody has chosen.
